source_receipt.locator: p.2 §2 Contextualized representations with Transformers; p.3 §3.1–3.2 and equation (3); p.4 §3.3 Fine-tuning
small_supporting_excerpts: Instead of fixed positional embeddings which encode absolute positional information, we use a convolutional layer ... which acts as relative positional embedding.

During pre-training, we learn representations of speech audio by solving a contrastive task ... which requires to identify the true quantized latent speech representation for a masked time step within a set of distractors.
Pre-trained models are fine-tuned for speech recognition by adding a randomly initialized linear projection ... Models are optimized by minimizing a CTC loss.
source_receipt.inspection_conclusion: The original method uses relative temporal positions and self-supervised masked latent contrastive pretraining without before/after answer labels. This refutes treating such labels as a universal requirement for time-aware representation learning; it does not prove this method or the course model can answer the tone-order question. The current lesson explicitly chooses supervised teaching of the order answer, which is a narrower task-design statement.

torch_api_additional_read.supporting_excerpt: Returns a new tensor with the natural logarithm of the elements of input. y_i = log_e(x_i). mean reduces the specified dimension.

mathematical_derivation: For positive powers P1,P2 above the floor, mean(log(P))=0.5*(ln(P1)+ln(P2))=ln(sqrt(P1*P2)). Thus (1,9) and (3,3) both give ln(3), while raw sums are 10 and 6. The mean-log feature cannot in general determine total power; no floor clipping is active in the example. The current code computes clamp/log before the later sequence.mean(0), consistent with the corrected name.
